FINANCIAL RESULTS | FINANZERGEBNISSE

Novartis delivered sales growth and core margin expansion in Q3; raised FY core operating income guidance

 

Ad hoc announcement pursuant to Art. 53 LR

 

Third quarter

·Q3 net sales grew +4% (cc1, +4% USD), with core operating income1 +10% (cc, +11% USD)
oSales growth driven by priority brands including Kisqali (+37% cc), Kesimpta (+22% cc), Scemblix (+67% cc), Leqvio (+63% cc) and Cosentyx (+9% cc)
oCore operating income margin1 was 41.6%, +2 percentage points (cc)
·Q3 operating income declined -61% (cc, -59% USD) mainly due to a partial impairment of the del-desiran asset; net income down -71% (cc, -70% USD)
·Q3 core EPS1 grew +8% (cc, +9% USD) to USD 2.46
·Q3 free cash flow1 was USD 5.1 billion (-18% USD)
·9 months net sales (0% cc, +2% USD) and core operating income (-2% cc, -1% USD) broadly in line with PY
·Q3 selected innovation milestones:
oRemibrutinib positive PhIII REMODEL-1 and -2 results in RMS
oRhapsido FDA approval in most prevalent form of CIndU
oPluvicto FDA and CN approvals in mAPMN/S prostate cancer
oPelabresib EU submission completed in MF
oDel-zota FDA priority review granted for DMD44
·Full-year 2026 guidance2 raised for core operating income
oNet sales expected to grow low single-digit (unchanged)
oCore operating income expected to be in line to grow low single-digit (from decline low single-digit)

  

Basel, October 27, 2026 – Commenting on Q3 2026 results, Vas Narasimhan, CEO of Novartis, said:

“Novartis delivered solid sales growth in Q3, as priority brands and launches more than offset generic erosion, demonstrating the replacement power of the business. Combined with productivity efforts, this drove strong bottom-line performance and allowed us to upgrade our full-year guidance. At the same time, we continued to advance our pipeline, with positive Phase III results for remibrutinib in RMS, label expansions for Rhapsido and Pluvicto in the US, and the first submission for pelabresib in the EU. While the del-desiran readout in DM1 was not what we had hoped, we saw evidence of clinical activity in the data and are working through the development path for this medicine. Importantly, our programs in FSHD and DMD continue to progress well. With continued momentum across the business and pipeline, we remain well on track to deliver our mid- and long-term outlook.”

Strategy

Our focus

 

Novartis is a “pure-play” innovative medicines company. We have a clear focus on four core therapeutic areas (cardiovascular-renal-metabolic, immunology, neuroscience and oncology), with multiple significant in-market and pipeline assets in each of these areas, that address high disease burden and have substantial growth potential. In addition to two established technology platforms (chemistry and biotherapeutics), three emerging platforms (gene & cell therapy, radioligand therapy and xRNA) are being prioritized for continued investment into new R&D capabilities and manufacturing scale. Geographically, we are focused on growing in our priority geographies – the US, China, Germany and Japan.

 

Our priorities

 

1.Accelerate growth: Renewed attention to deliver high-value medicines (NMEs) and focus on launch excellence, with a rich pipeline across our core therapeutic areas.
2.Deliver returns: Continuing to embed operational excellence and deliver improved financials. Novartis remains disciplined and shareholder-focused in our approach to capital allocation, with substantial cash generation and a strong capital structure supporting continued flexibility.
3.Strengthen foundations: Unleashing the power of our people, scaling data science and technology, and continuing to build trust with society.

 

Financials

 

Third quarter

 

Net sales were USD 14.5 billion (+4%, +4% cc), with volume growth contributing 14 percentage points, partly offset by 9 percentage points from generic competition. Pricing had a negative impact of 1 percentage point, and currency had no impact.

 

Operating income was USD 1.8 billion (-59%, -61% cc), declining mainly due to higher R&D expenses, including a USD 1.9 billion partial impairment charge of the del-desiran IPR&D asset, and higher other expense, partly offset by higher net sales.

 

Net income was USD 1.2 billion (-70%, -71% cc), declining mainly due to lower operating income and higher interest expense. EPS was USD 0.63 (-69%, -70% cc).

 

Core operating income was USD 6.0 billion (+11%, +10% cc), mainly driven by higher net sales. Core operating income margin was 41.6% of net sales, increasing 2.3 percentage points (2.0 percentage points in cc).

 

Core net income was USD 4.7 billion (+8%, +6% cc), driven by higher core operating income, partly offset by higher interest expense. Core EPS was USD 2.46 (+9%, +8% cc), benefiting from the lower weighted average number of shares outstanding.

 

Free cash flow amounted to USD 5.1 billion (-18%), declining due to lower net cash flows from operating activities.

 

Nine months

 

Net sales were USD 42.0 billion (+2%, 0% cc), with volume growth contributing 14 percentage points, partly offset by 12 percentage points from generic competition. Pricing had a negative impact of 2 percentage points, and currency had a positive impact of 2 percentage points.

 

Operating income was USD 10.8 billion (-23%, -24% cc), declining mainly due to higher R&D expenses, including a USD 1.9 billion partial impairment charge of the del-desiran IPR&D asset, and higher other expense.

 

2
 

 

 

 

Net income was USD 7.6 billion (-34%, -35% cc), mainly due to lower operating income, higher interest expense and higher income taxes. EPS was USD 4.01 (-32%, -33% cc).

 

Core operating income was USD 16.9 billion (-1%, -2% cc), declining mainly due to higher R&D expenses and higher other expense, partly offset by lower SG&A expenses. Core operating income margin was 40.1% of net sales, decreasing 1.1 percentage points (0.8 percentage points in cc).

 

Core net income was USD 13.0 billion (-4%, -5% cc), mainly due to lower core operating income and higher interest expense. Core EPS was USD 6.85 (-1%, -3% cc), benefiting from the lower weighted average number of shares outstanding.

 

Free cash flow amounted to USD 14.0 billion (-12%), declining due to lower net cash flows from operating activities.

 

Q3 priority brands

 

Underpinning our financial results in the quarter is a continued focus on key growth drivers (ranked in order of contribution to Q3 growth) including:

 

Kisqali

 (USD 1 821 million, +37% cc) continued to grow strongly across all regions, with market share growth in early breast cancer and leadership in metastatic breast cancer.
Kesimpta (USD 1 484 million, +22% cc) sales showed continued strong momentum globally, driven by increased demand and broad access.
Scemblix

(USD 593 million, +67% cc) sales grew across all regions, with continued strong momentum in the early-line setting in the US, Japan and Germany.

Leqvio (USD 506 million, +63% cc) sales grew across all regions, with continued uptake in China following NRDL inclusion.
Cosentyx (USD 1 857 million, +9% cc) sales grew in most markets, driven by the HS and SpA indications. US growth benefited from prior-year revenue deduction adjustments.
Pluvicto (USD 674 million, +20% cc) sales showed continued strong demand driven by the mAPMR1 setting, with US and China approvals in mAPMN/S2 in Q3, and ongoing access expansion ex-US.
Zolgensma Group (USD 404 million, +35% cc) sales grew strongly, reflecting continued launch momentum from Itvisma in the US, Japan and other ex-US countries.
Rhapsido (USD 101 million) continued to show strong launch uptake in the US, supported by sustained prescription growth and a free drug program facilitating patient access. Ex-US, sales were mainly driven by early launch uptake in Germany and China.
Fabhalta (USD 237 million, +60% cc) sales grew, with expansion in PNH and renal indications.

R&D update – key developments from the third quarter

 

New approvals

Rhapsido

(remibrutinib)

 In October, FDA approved Rhapsido as the first treatment for adults with symptomatic dermographism (SD) inadequately controlled by H1 antihistamines, expanding its use beyond chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) into chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU). Novartis plans to submit the full RemIND dataset to health authorities globally.

Pluvicto

(lutetium Lu177 vipivotide tetraxetan)

 FDA and China’s NMPA approved Pluvicto in combination with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) for patients with PSMA+ metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive/sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer1. Pluvicto is now approved across all stages of PSMA+ metastatic prostate cancer.

Fabhalta

(iptacopan)

Japan’s MHLW approved Fabhalta for the treatment of IgA nephropathy (IgAN), making it the first approved treatment for this indication in Japan.

 

Additionally, FDA granted traditional approval of Fabhalta in IgAN.

1 Also known as metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC).

Regulatory updates

Cosentyx

(secukinumab)

 CHMP adopted a positive opinion recommending approval for Cosentyx in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR), based on positive Phase III REPLENISH data. If approved, Cosentyx will be the first IL-17A inhibitor approved in Europe for PMR.

DAK539

(pelabresib)

 Regulatory submission for pelabresib in myelofibrosis was completed in the EU, based on the positive Phase III MANIFEST-2 study, which showed deep and durable disease control, with a safety profile comparable to ruxolitinib alone, including numerically fewer deaths and disease progressions in the pelabresib arm.

KPE179

(del-zota)

 Del-zota was granted priority review by FDA for people living with Duchenne muscular dystrophy who have a genetic variant that may be amenable to exon 44 skipping (DMD44). Del-zota previously received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation.

Leqvio

(inclisiran)

 FDA updated the Leqvio label to include language recognizing that lowering LDL-C reduces the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in adults at increased cardiovascular risk. This update reflects established evidence from statins and monoclonal antibody PCSK9 inhibitors, supporting LDL-C reduction as a key component of cardiovascular risk management.

Vanrafia

(atrasentan)

 Regulatory submissions for Vanrafia in IgAN were completed in Japan and China.
KLU156
(ganaplacide + lumefantrine)		 Regulatory submission for KLU156 in uncomplicated malaria was completed in the US and received priority review.

 

 

Results from ongoing trials and other highlights  

LOU064
(remibrutinib)		 Positive results from the Phase III REMODEL-1 and -2 trials showed oral remibrutinib met its primary endpoint in relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS), significantly reducing annualized relapse rate (ARR) versus teriflunomide. Remibrutinib also showed superiority on all key secondary endpoints, including MRI lesion reduction, and a clinically meaningful delay in disability progression. The safety profile was favorable and consistent with remibrutinib in CSU, with no liver safety signal. Data were presented at MSToronto2026 in October.

EWF980

(del-desiran)

 In the Phase III HARBOR study, del-desiran did not meet its primary endpoint of video hand opening time (vHOT) versus placebo in myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1). Evidence of clinical activity was observed in secondary endpoints and exploratory analyses. Novartis is evaluating the full HARBOR dataset and will engage with health authorities to determine the most appropriate development path. Data will be presented at an upcoming medical congress.

TQJ230

(pelacarsen)

 In the Phase III HORIZON trial, pelacarsen did not meet its primary endpoint of reducing the risk of cardiovascular events versus placebo in patients with elevated Lp(a) and established cardiovascular disease (CVD), despite reducing Lp(a) levels in this study population. The findings provide important new evidence on the relationship between Lp(a) lowering and cardiovascular outcomes and may help inform future approaches to cardiovascular risk management. Data will be presented at an upcoming medical congress.
Kisqali
(ribociclib) 		The six-year follow-up analysis of the Phase III NATALEE trial showed a clinically meaningful overall survival (OS) benefit with Kisqali plus endocrine therapy (ET) versus ET alone in the broadest HR+/HER2- early breast cancer (eBC) population at high risk of recurrence, reducing the risk of death by nearly 20%. Patients had been off Kisqali treatment for a median of 38 months, with clinical benefit continuing to deepen

 

 

5
 

 

 

 

 after treatment completion. The safety profile remained consistent with previous analyses. Data were presented at ESMO 2026.

LOU064

(remibrutinib)

 Novartis has discontinued the Phase III study of remibrutinib in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) following a futility analysis, which indicated the treatment was unlikely to meet its efficacy objectives. No safety concerns were identified, and there is no impact on remibrutinib studies in other indications.
Selected transactions

Novartis completed the acquisition of Myricx Bio, strengthening the oncology pipeline with a new class of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), including two lead assets targeting B7-H3 and HER2, as well as a broader payload platform with potential impact across multiple solid tumor settings.

 

Novartis exercised its exclusive option to acquire full global rights to Sironax's proprietary Brain Delivery Module (BDM) platform, a next-generation blood-brain barrier crossing technology with the potential to transform the treatment of central nervous system diseases.

 

Novartis entered into an exclusive global licensing agreement with BoomRay Pharmaceuticals for an undisclosed preclinical radioligand therapy asset, further strengthening its radioligand therapy portfolio.

 

In October, Novartis entered into a strategic licensing and option agreement with Abogen Biosciences to advance RNA-encoded therapeutics, including an exclusive worldwide license to ABO2203, a novel mRNA-encoded CD19xCD3 T-cell engager with the potential to transform the treatment landscape for autoimmune diseases. The transaction is subject to the completion of customary closing conditions.

  

Capital structure and net debt

 

Retaining a good balance between investment in the business, a strong capital structure, and attractive shareholder returns remains a priority.

 

During the first nine months of 2026, Novartis repurchased 30.9 million shares for USD 4.7 billion on the SIX Swiss Exchange second trading line. These repurchases included 18.8 million shares (USD 2.8 billion) under the up-to USD 10 billion share buyback announced in July 2025 (with up to USD 4.9 billion still to be executed). In addition, 12.1 million shares (USD 1.8 billion) were repurchased to mitigate the anticipated full-year dilution related to participation plans of employees. Further, 2.0 million shares (USD 0.3 billion) were repurchased from employees. During the same period, USD 0.9 billion of equity-based compensation plan expenses were recognized to equity and 13.3 million shares were delivered to employees related to equity-based compensation plans from prior years. As a result, the total number of shares outstanding decreased by 19.6 million compared with December 31, 2025. These treasury share transactions resulted in an equity decrease of USD 4.1 billion and a cash outflow of USD 4.8 billion.

 

Net debt increased to USD 37.4 billion at September 30, 2026, compared with USD 21.9 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase was mainly due to the free cash flow of USD 14.0 billion being more than offset by the net cash outflow for M&A, intangible assets transactions and other acquisitions of USD 16.7 billion, the USD 9.1 billion annual dividend payment and cash outflows for treasury share transactions of USD 4.8 billion.

 

As of Q3 2026, the long-term credit rating for the company is Aa3 with Moody’s Ratings and AA- with S&P Global Ratings.

Foreign exchange impact

The estimated impact of exchange rates on our results is provided monthly on our website.

 

2027 Annual General Meeting

 

Nomination for election to the Board of Directors

 

The Novartis Board of Directors announced today that it is nominating Rajesh Jha for election to the Board. During a 36-year career at Microsoft, Mr. Jha held a series of senior leadership roles across software engineering, productivity platforms and enterprise technologies, and served on the company's Senior Leadership Team from 2016 until his retirement. Most recently, he served as Executive Vice President, Experiences + Devices, where he led the product teams for Microsoft 365, Office, Teams, Windows + Devices, and Dynamics, and played a key role in the integration of artificial intelligence across Microsoft's product portfolio. His extensive experience in technology, AI and large-scale digital platforms would add significantly to the Novartis Board of Directors.
